name: Watermelon Powdery Mildew
description: A fungal disease causing white powdery growth on watermelon leaves and stems. It reduces photosynthetic capacity and can cause premature defoliation, leading to sunscalded fruit and yield loss.
symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on upper leaf surfaces
Yellowing and necrosis of affected leaves
Fruit sunscald due to loss of leaf cover
causes: Dense vine canopy with poor air circulation
treatments: Apply sulfur-based fungicides at first sign of infection
Spray neem oil solution (5ml/L water) weekly
Use trifloxystrobin or myclobutanil for severe infections
Apply potassium bicarbonate as organic alternative
prevention: Space plants adequately for air circulation
Avoid overhead irrigation — use drip irrigation
Remove and destroy infected vine debris after harvest
Practice crop rotation with non-cucurbit crops
